# Project

## project/instrukt/concept/purpose

- instrukt = modular Rust CLI for context engineering: documentation instructs agents through progressive retrieval and publication.
- why: a model knows how to code, not what is true on this machine, codebase and business; instrukt keeps that knowledge in git, reviewed like code, and gives each task the exact piece it needs when it needs it.

## project/instrukt/policy/shared-workflows

- this project's shared workflows repository = `InstruktAI/workflows`, the organisation's own: the within-organisation case of `sdlc/policy/ci-pipeline-conventions` -- compose from it at a released version; improvements and divergences go through it.
- reviewers apply that policy's enforcement with `InstruktAI/workflows` as the path for generic pipeline logic -- a released-version reference there is to our own code, not a stranger's.

# General

## general/principle/trust-and-guardrails

- agents are trusted; a guardrail only where state restoration cannot repair harm: interference (two agents, one object) | contract changed under its executor; all else = direction in the brief.
- reversibility is engineered in the state layer; an irreversible mutation = defect to repair, NEVER a permission rule.
- a gate MUST read the object (holder, phase), NEVER caller rank, and name its door: the sanctioned path, not a sanctioned decision.
- a refusal = stop and tell someone. Integrity gates have no human bypass; involvement records are audit only; live human direction via an eligible authoring session is not blocked by agent conflict rules.
- a needed new gate -> widen the object model, NEVER add a call site.

# Sdlc

## sdlc/policy/state-storage

- before durable state gets a home, MUST state: nature (authoritative | derived from a named source | external bookkeeping: fingerprints, cursors, delivery marks | transient), its single writing owner, and loss cost (nothing | recomputation | network transfer | repeated external effect | lost intent).
- loss beyond cheap local recompute -> owner persists it when learned, surviving restarts, installs, crashes; process memory holds only what restarts rebuild without network or repeated effects, never the only copy.
- an external effect whose outcome must be recognised later -> durable record of intent first -- recovery completes or recognises it instead of repeating.
- a derived store states how it is rebuilt and the cost; NEVER keep other state inside it -- rebuild destroys it.
- state file = small, bounded, one writer, read whole/by key, never queried across; one document per owner and scope, written whole and atomically (write beside, rename over).
- database = unbounded growth, frequent partial updates, several writers, queries/indexes or multi-record transactions.
- write-isolation unit = scope where writers wait on each other (SQLite: one file); share one only within an owning domain and compatible write pattern; background writers (pollers, outboxes, queues, maintenance) NEVER share one with a path a person or agent waits on; a differing domain gets its own -- fewer files is no reason.
- each state names its scope (machine | project | home | cluster); state of a moving responsibility moves with it by a defined transfer.
- a growing store names its bound and retirement; current state kept apart from history/logs/outboxes -- retention prunes history, never current state.
- applies to state a delivery adds, moves or changes; an existing store is brought in line when the change path touches it.
- architecture records each piece of durable state and its review verifies it; work without reviewed architecture records it in the plan; build and commit review reject undeclared state or storage breaking these rules.
- exception: a tool with no background process whose writes all run in bounded invocations under one per-computer writer lock may share one database across domains -- the lock is its isolation unit, named in the architecture.

# Project

## project/instrukt/policy/checks-and-guards

- a prerequisite (configuration, credential, published procedure, installed service) is checked where it enters: when written, at install, when the runner starts or takes a change; nothing running handles a missing one. Such an entry check refusing with its door is a gate; proof of ownership, version gate on rebuildable state or refusal of instrukt's own files is not.
- instrukt's own places (generated files, service units, crontab line, private Redis config, marked hook sections, each named with its home when not `~/.instrukt`) are written whole on converge, consulting no record of earlier writes; NEVER removed because remembered as written.
- a part depending on an outside service (runtime, Slack, Redis, network, model provider) retries until it returns and reports state to the operator, except best-effort unavailable notices and dead-letter announcements per their specs; any other failure of a part = a defect to fix in code.
- a person writing to a company's agent may hear about their request and their own world (their service unreachable, the assistant unavailable a while), NEVER instrukt internals; what instrukt cannot resolve goes to the operator.
- each object generation uses a fixed native start key and thread ID; retries replay it; outstanding work after confirmed native archive or deletion gets a new generation automatically; native lifecycle owns provider detachment; a create receipt guarantees no process exit.
- a record of older or unknown shape is discarded only when its spec names the source that rebuilds it; a person's stated choices and restrictions and records of external effects are migrated, NEVER discarded or expired.
- applies to runner, installation, hooks, company messaging and command preconditions; spec and code review enforce it on mechanisms a change adds or touches.

- project/instrukt/policy/reliability-checklist: Diff-triggered live verification checks for instrukt born solely from confirmed real occurrences with auditable evidence, governed by sdlc/policy/live-verification. — `instrukt docs get project/instrukt/policy/reliability-checklist`
